Materials

Five partition materials

Every material for every environment. Each one is built differently, and that decides where it fits.

Compare all materials

Powder coated steel

Galvannealed steel faces over a honeycomb core.

Fits: Offices and other dry restrooms where budget matters.

Learn more

Solid plastic (HDPE)

One solid sheet of high-density polyethylene.

Fits: Moisture, mildew and graffiti resistance. Ask for a fire-rated grade where the code requires it.

Learn more

Phenolic

Layers of resin-soaked kraft paper fused into one dense sheet.

Fits: Wet areas and high-traffic restrooms.

Learn more

Plastic laminate

High-pressure laminate bonded to a particleboard core.

Fits: Dry restrooms where color and pattern choice matter.

Learn more

Stainless steel

Type 304 stainless faces over a honeycomb core.

Fits: Restrooms where corrosion resistance and a premium finish matter.

Learn more

Not sure which fits? See what bathroom partitions are made of.

Mounting styles

Four ways to mount them

Mounting is separate from material. It decides what your floor and ceiling have to provide.

Compare mounting styles

Overhead braced

Floor-anchored pilasters tied together by a headrail. The general-purpose style.

See details

Floor mounted

Pilasters bolted into the floor with no headrail. Needs structural concrete.

See details

Ceiling hung

Pilasters hang from structural steel above the ceiling, so nothing touches the floor.

See details

Floor to ceiling

Pilasters anchored into the floor and the ceiling structure.

See details

Before you order

Good to know

What is included with the partitions

A partition system is more than panels. Our quotes include panels, doors, pilasters, hinges, slide latches, keepers, strikes, brackets, pilaster shoes and mounting fasteners, plus headrails where the mounting style uses them. Nothing to source separately. Hardware is often a different material from the panels, so tell us if you need a particular finish. See hardware & parts for replacement hinges, latches, doors and brackets for stalls you already own.

Measuring for a quote

A few measurements make the quote faster: room width along the stall wall, room depth, ceiling height and toilet centerlines. Our stall dimensions guide and restroom layout guide show what to measure. Photos of the floor, walls and ceiling help too.

Accessible stalls

Accessible stall sizing is available in every material. Under the 2010 ADA Standards, a wheelchair-accessible compartment is at least 60 inches wide, with a door that gives at least 32 inches of clear opening (604.8.1.1, 404.2.3). Compliance depends on the whole restroom, so confirm it with your architect or code official. See the ADA compliance guide.

Disclaimer: ADA dimensions and accessibility guidance shown here are provided for general informational purposes only. Codes and their interpretation vary by jurisdiction and project. We accept no responsibility or liability for compliance — always verify requirements with your architect, engineer, or local code official before ordering.

Installation

Next Partitions supplies the partitions. You arrange installation. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and the approved drawings, and use a qualified installer.
